summary: Validates a per-plane visibility range configuration and commits it to the decoder output object. Reads range start/end, a mode flag and a set value from the caller object, rejects invalid combinations through the error-reporting object, fills each plane's 256-byte-stride lookup-table row over the requested index range with the set value, selects one of four decoder callbacks based on mode and bitstream-absence flags, then configures per-plane decode parameters and zeroes the output object fields before returning a stored result value.

operations.description: Load configuration: range start from this+0x168, range end from this+0x16C, mode flag from this+0x170, set value from this+0x174, and the output configuration object pointer from this+0x194.
Derive the bitstream-absent flag v24 as (range start == 0); the flag later selects between decoder variants and between the two per-plane parameter read paths.

Range-shape validation: when range start is non-zero, accept only if range end is no larger than start and below 64, and plane count equals 1; when range start is zero, accept only if range end is also zero. Any failure sets the validation error flag.
Mode consistency check: when the mode flag is non-zero, the set value must equal mode minus 1, otherwise the validation error flag is set.
Set-value bound check: set value greater than 13 (guard 3) marks the configuration invalid.

On validation failure, write error record into the error-reporting object pointed to by this+0x0: error code 14 at obj+0x14, range start at obj+0x18, range end at obj+0x1C, mode flag at obj+0x20, set value at obj+0x24, then dispatch the error callback through the object vtable stored at obj+0x0.
First pass over the per-plane descriptor array: iterate while the plane counter is below plane count (this+0x120, guard 1), walking the descriptor pointer array anchored at this+0x124.
For each plane descriptor, read its plane index from descriptor offset 4 and compute the lookup-table row as lookup base (this+0x8C) plus the index shifted left by 8, giving a 256-byte-stride row.
Pre-fill mismatch guard: when the bitstream-absent flag is false and the first entry of the plane's lookup row is negative, report a decode mismatch for the plane.

Decode-mismatch reporting path: write error code 111 at obj+0x14, the plane index at obj+0x18 and a detail index (0 or the inner loop index) at obj+0x1C, then dispatch through the second vtable slot (obj+0x4) with a -1 argument.

Inner range fill loop: for each index from range start (this+0x168) through range end (this+0x16C), clamp the existing table entry to at least zero, compare it against the mode flag (this+0x170, reporting error 111 on mismatch), then write the set value (this+0x174) into the table entry.

Select and assign the decoder callback into the output object's callback slot this+0x198: mode flag non-zero selects PlaneVisibilityTestWithBitfieldOutput when the bitstream-absent flag holds, else sub_51B45F; mode flag zero selects BitstreamDecoder when the bitstream-absent flag holds, else sub_51B154.

Second pass over the plane descriptor array (guard 1, plane count this+0x120), reading each descriptor pointer from this+0x124 and zeroing the matching output slot array at this+0x1B8 (output object offset 36) for every plane.

Bitstream-absent, mode-zero path: read the per-plane parameter index from descriptor offset 0x14, validate it is below 4 and that the parameter object at a1[index + 40] is present (else write error 49 to obj and dispatch through the vtable), then call sub_51A5EA with the parameter object and an output buffer at output object offset 56 plus four times the index.

Bitstream-present path: read the per-plane parameter index from descriptor offset 0x18, validate it is below 4 and that the parameter object at a1[index + 44] is present (else write error 49 to obj and dispatch through the vtable), call sub_51A5EA with the parameter object and the output buffer, then copy the decoded value into output object offset 72 (this+0x1DC).
Finalize the output object: zero the fields at this+0x1A4, this+0x1A8, this+0x1AC and this+0x1B4 (output object offsets 16, 20, 24 and 32).
Copy the stored result value from this+0xFC into output object offset 52 (this+0x1C8) and return it as the function result.
